decision.label: ANSWER
decision.response: Yes. The manual states that in rainfed agriculture the beginning of the rainy period (June–July) is the favourable planting period, and if there is a possibility to supplement by irrigation, garlic can be planted in August. So August planting is supported only where you can supplement soil moisture with irrigation; otherwise the manual does not support August planting.
decision.justification: Page 11 (section 3.6 Planting time) states: 'In rain fed agriculture the beginning of the rainy period (June-July) is the favourable period and if there is possibility to supplement by irrigation it can be planted in August.' The answer is conditional on irrigation, which the farmer must confirm; no other dates or doses are added.
